In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like NVDA near its 52-week high with elevated realised volatility and a surging oil backdrop, the median 5-session forward return was 0.86%. The distribution is wide, with a standard deviation of 3.8% and a 10th percentile of -4.04%, meaning the single number to anchor on is that roughly one in ten similar weeks ended down more than 4%.

[state]
The engine pulled these analogs because NVDA sits -6.03% from its 52-week high (z-score 0.564) while running hot: 20-session realised volatility is 45.77% (z-score 0.824), mean absolute overnight/weekend gaps are 1.28% (z-score 0.718), and WTI crude has surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124). Simultaneously, dollar volume is thin at a z-score of -0.62, and benchmark volatility is unusually low at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). This combination of idiosyncratic heat, macro commodity shock, and quiet broad markets pulls in Technology names alongside Energy and ETF Sector analogs. Headlines framing the session include CNBC Markets noting "Stock futures are flat as investors grapple with higher yields, await Fed minutes" and "Surging Treasury yields don’t signal a U.S. 'fiscal apocalypse' — yet." Derivatives positioning data is unavailable on this card.

[history]
Over the next 5 sessions, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 0.65% and a median of 0.86%, with outcomes ranging from -7.34% to 10.25%. The distribution carries a slight positive skew of 0.214, but 44% of episodes finished below zero. The bad tail is dominated by specific names: the closest analog, NVDA itself on 2026-09-08, fell -5.9% with a max adverse excursion of -7.44%. XLK on 2026-08-13 dropped -4.02%. Conversely, NVDA on 2025-06-20 rallied 9.66%, and MU on 2024-01-16 gained 3.45%. Only 3 of the 50 analogs are NVDA; the rest span 33 distinct symbols, heavily weighted toward recent dates, with 22 from 2026 and 16 from 2025.

[tails]
A position can end the week near flat while being un-holdable intra-week. The median maximum adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -2.01%, while the 10th percentile adverse excursion reached -4.38%. In 8% of the retrieved episodes, the path breached a 5% drawdown at some point during the 5 sessions. No episode in this set breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown threshold. The median maximum favourable excursion was 2.55%, yielding a reward-to-risk ratio of 1.27 based on the excursion medians.

[stress]
The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario is the most severe, dropping the median forward return to -5.4% (a delta of -6.26% versus baseline) using 48 analogs, with a 58.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; however, central-bank backstops arrived inside that window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produced a median of -3.02% across 50 analogs, but it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019 which flatters late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear yielded a median of -2.42% across 50 analogs, though a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind showed a median of -2.11% across 36 analogs, but the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2025-04 tariff shock delivered a median of -2.7% across 26 analogs, with policy reversals inside the window making the tail asymmetric. The volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) resulted in a median of -0.18% across 50 analogs, but VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The liquidity air pocket scenario returned a median of 0.83% across 50 analogs, but gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue; for the verified Bitget RWA perpetual, the reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week and 54.59% of realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours. The earnings day, FOMC day, crypto contagion, China ADR de-rating, rates-up, regional banks 2023, and weekend-hold scenarios all produced medians between -0.39% and 1.61%, each carrying their respective caveats regarding small sample sizes, structural risks not captured in price features, or deterministic block pairing conventions. No scenarios were skipped.
